title: Watch your cashflow, revenue pulled in
caption: You do not need more revenue. You need revenue earlier.

predicted-revenue-does-not-count.description: Revenue that is only predicted is discounted by investors, and founders who rely on raising more money often find that assumption false.[1]

default-alive-or-default-dead.title: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead?

same-board-earlier-revenue.title: Same board, earlier revenue
same-board-earlier-revenue.keywords: first board, same costs, revenue back to February, stays positive, no stamp
same-board-earlier-revenue.script: Now back to our first board. Same notes, same costs. This time, I drag April's revenue back two months, to February. The cash note after February no longer reads zero. It stays positive. No bankrupt stamp. The story flips.

not-more-earlier.title: Not more, earlier
not-more-earlier.keywords: not a cent more, revenue moved to the costs, the whole game, earlier
not-more-earlier.script: Look at what changed. The company did not earn a cent more. Its revenue moved to the month where the costs were. That is the whole game. You do not need more revenue. You need revenue earlier.

how-it-moves.title: How it moves
how-it-moves.keywords: not by wishing, earlier sales, sales takes time, next part
how-it-moves.script: But revenue does not move by wishing. Earlier revenue only comes from earlier sales. And sales takes time. That is why the next part is about time.
